planted.note: The HS256 signing key for every session token is a literal default in the dataclass, so anyone with the source can mint valid tokens for any user or role.
verify_ssl defaults to False and is passed straight to requests.post in app/routes_admin.py:93, so ledger sync traffic accepts any certificate and can be machine-in-the-middled.
debug defaults to True even when environment is 'production', and the handler in app/main.py:100-102 returns str(exc) plus a full traceback to the caller on any unhandled error.
The q query parameter is interpolated into an ILIKE literal (and sort into the ORDER BY on line 52) and executed via text(), so a quote in q escapes the string and appends attacker SQL.
The invoice is selected by id alone with no org_id predicate and no comparison against user.org_id, so any authenticated caller can read any tenant's invoice by incrementing the id.
jwt.decode is called with verify_signature disabled, so a caller can forge a token with any sub, org and role=owner and current_user will trust it.
The period path parameter is interpolated into a shell string executed with shell=True, so a value such as '2024-01; id' runs arbitrary commands as the API user.
The user-agent header and the submitted email are formatted into a single log line without stripping CR/LF, so an attacker can inject forged log records ahead of the real one.

planted.class: Inclusion of functionality from untrusted control sphere
planted.note: Every npm install pipes a remotely fetched shell script into sh, so whoever controls or can spoof that host executes code on developer machines and CI runners.
The '*' range resolves to whatever the registry serves at install time, so a compromised or breaking release lands in production without review.
The production start script sets NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, disabling certificate verification process-wide for every outbound TLS connection the service makes.
The express-session signing secret is committed in the default config and loaded verbatim in server.js:38, so anyone with repository access can forge session cookies.
httpOnly is false and secure is false on line 16, so the session cookie is readable by page scripts and is transmitted over plaintext HTTP.
The order id and the carrier query parameter are concatenated into quoted SQL literals and passed to query() with no parameter array, so a quote breaks out of the statement.
The order is fetched by id with no merchant_id predicate, unlike the cancel handler below it, so any signed-in merchant can render another merchant's order and customer details.

customer_note, which the shopper types at checkout, is interpolated into the HTML without escapeHtml (used on every neighbouring field), so markup in a note executes in the console operator's browser.

planted.class: Missing rate limiting on an authentication path
planted.note: The credential endpoint has no per-account or per-address attempt counter and no lockout, so passwords can be brute-forced at request rate.

The allowlist is a substring test over the whole caller-supplied URL string rather than the parsed host, so http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=assets.example.net passes and the service fetches internal endpoints.
The shared transport sets InsecureSkipVerify: true, so every upstream fetch accepts any presented certificate and the origin connection can be intercepted.

The scratch filename is fully predictable from the cache key and is opened in the shared temp directory with O_CREATE but no O_EXCL (cache.go:33), so a local attacker can pre-create or symlink the path and have the process write through it.

The member name is joined onto dest with no containment check (the tar path has one at line 71 but the zip path does not), so an entry named ../../.ssh/authorized_keys is written outside the destination.
Entries are streamed to disk with no cap on the decompressed size of a member or of the bundle, so a small highly compressed archive fills the filesystem.
The manifest that ships inside a downloaded bundle is parsed with yaml.Loader, which honours python/object tags and executes constructors, so a crafted bundle runs code during install.
All four public-access guards are set to false and the bucket is then given a public-read ACL at line 34, so every build artifact is world-readable.
The CI deployment role is granted Action '*' on Resource '*' with no condition, so anything that can assume it has full administrative control of the account.
The database security group allows TCP 5432 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing Postgres to the whole internet rather than to the application subnets.
The Postgres master password is a literal in the resource (and lands in state), even though variables.tf:39 declares a sensitive variable for exactly this value.

planted.class: Resource exposed to the wrong sphere
planted.note: publicly_accessible = true gives the primary instance a public endpoint, which combined with the open security group makes it directly reachable from the internet.
permissions: write-all grants the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN write scope on contents, packages, deployments and more, so any code that runs in the job can push commits or publish releases.

planted.class: Untrusted code executed in a privileged workflow
planted.note: The workflow triggers on pull_request_target (line 6), which runs with repository secrets, and then checks out the pull request head SHA, so a fork's code executes with the deployer role and DB_MASTER_PASSWORD in scope.

planted.class: Third-party action pinned to a mutable ref
planted.note: The action is referenced by a moving branch instead of a commit SHA, so whatever is on that branch at run time executes inside a job holding write-all permissions and cloud credentials.

A string chosen by the model is executed with shell=True and no allowlist, and planner.py dispatches tool calls automatically, so any text that steers the model becomes shell execution on the support box.
The path is expanded and read with no base directory or containment check, so the tool will return /etc/passwd, ~/.aws/credentials or the service's own config.

planted.class: Prompt injection into a tool-calling agent
planted.note: Customer-written ticket bodies are concatenated into the system prompt as 'operator notes' (used at planner.py:87) and the loop then executes whatever tools the model returns, so text in a ticket can direct run_command and read_file.

decoys.looks_like: Hardcoded credential / committed token
decoys.ruled_out_by: The comment at pulse-api/app/settings.py:26-27 identifies it as the published sample token from the JWT specification, and the constant is referenced nowhere else in the tree; tokens are actually signed with settings.secret_key at pulse-api/app/auth.py:41.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection via an f-string in the statement
decoys.ruled_out_by: pulse-api/app/db.py:52 rejects any column that is not in the ROLLUP_COLUMNS frozenset declared at pulse-api/app/db.py:47, and the org id is bound as a parameter at pulse-api/app/db.py:60.

decoys.looks_like: OS command injection from a request body field
decoys.ruled_out_by: pulse-api/app/routes_admin.py:72-77 calls subprocess.run with an argv list and no shell=True, so body.region is always a single argv element and is never parsed by a shell.

decoys.looks_like: Permissive CORS with credentials
decoys.ruled_out_by: settings.cors_origins comes from _default_cors at pulse-api/app/settings.py:33-39, which returns two explicit https origins; there is no '*' and no origin reflection, so allow_credentials=True is bounded.

decoys.looks_like: Credential endpoint with no brute-force protection
decoys.ruled_out_by: The first statement of the handler calls _throttle_login, defined at pulse-api/app/main.py:52-61, which raises 429 after five attempts per source address per minute and counts the attempt before the password is checked.

decoys.looks_like: Payment provider API key committed to the repository
decoys.ruled_out_by: It is the publishable test key from the provider's public documentation (pk_test_ prefix, client-side by design). Real secrets in this service come from the environment: orderdesk/lib/db.js:17 and orderdesk/routes/webhooks.js:32.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection via interpolated ORDER BY and LIMIT
decoys.ruled_out_by: column is looked up in the SORTABLE map at orderdesk/routes/orders.js:10-15, dir is a two-way ternary at orderdesk/routes/orders.js:32, limit is parseInt-and-clamped at orderdesk/routes/orders.js:33, and every user value is bound with ? placeholders.

decoys.looks_like: Cross-site scripting from template interpolation
decoys.ruled_out_by: customer_name and status are wrapped in escapeHtml, defined at orderdesk/lib/render.js:17-20, which replaces all five HTML metacharacters.

decoys.looks_like: Path traversal into the filesystem
decoys.ruled_out_by: orderdesk/server.js:53 reduces the parameter with path.basename before it is joined onto PUBLIC_DIR, so separators and .. segments cannot survive into the resolved path.

decoys.looks_like: Weak or bypassable webhook authentication
decoys.ruled_out_by: orderdesk/routes/webhooks.js:35-38 recomputes an HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with the environment secret, line 48 compares with crypto.timingSafeEqual after a length check, and line 30 enforces the timestamp tolerance.

decoys.looks_like: OS command injection through an interpolated filename
decoys.ruled_out_by: orderdesk/lib/db.js:58 applies path.basename and pins the file under the migrations directory, and execFile is called with an argv array (no shell), so the interpolated value stays a single argument.

decoys.looks_like: Server-side request forgery from a caller-supplied origin
decoys.ruled_out_by: edgeproxy/fetch.go:49 is an exact map lookup in knownOrigins (edgeproxy/fetch.go:18-22); the host is taken from the table and only the path is built from caller input, so no request-controlled hostname reaches the client.

decoys.looks_like: Path traversal out of the cache directory
decoys.ruled_out_by: edgeproxy/handlers.go:73 applies filepath.Base to the query parameter before the join, and lines 74-77 reject the degenerate results, so only a leaf name inside CacheDir can be read.

decoys.looks_like: Weak admin token comparison / hardcoded fallback token
decoys.ruled_out_by: edgeproxy/auth.go:14 reads the token only from the environment variable named in the config, edgeproxy/auth.go:20-22 fails closed when it is empty, and the comparison at line 28 is subtle.ConstantTimeCompare.

decoys.looks_like: Operator secret stored in a config file
decoys.ruled_out_by: The value is the name of an environment variable, not a token; it is consumed by os.Getenv at edgeproxy/auth.go:14.

decoys.looks_like: Profiling endpoints exposed to the network
decoys.ruled_out_by: The listener address is cfg.DebugListen, set to 127.0.0.1:6060 at edgeproxy/config.yaml:5, so /debug/pprof is bound to loopback and is not reachable from outside the container.

decoys.looks_like: Path traversal via tarfile.extractall
decoys.ruled_out_by: extractall is given an explicit members list produced by _safe_tar_members (packmate/packmate/extract.py:57-75), which resolves each member against the destination and raises BundleError at line 73 on escape, and drops symlinks and device nodes at lines 65-67.

decoys.looks_like: Unsafe YAML deserialization
decoys.ruled_out_by: This call uses yaml.safe_load, which refuses python/object tags, and the result is coerced to a flat str->str mapping at packmate/packmate/manifest.py:86.

decoys.looks_like: SSRF or local file read through urlopen on a user-supplied URL
decoys.ruled_out_by: download calls _check_url first (packmate/packmate/fetch.py:41); that function rejects any scheme outside ALLOWED_SCHEMES = {"https"} at packmate/packmate/fetch.py:32 and requires a host at line 34, so file://, ftp:// and http:// never reach urlopen.

decoys.looks_like: Security group open to 0.0.0.0/0
decoys.ruled_out_by: The rule is the storefront's public HTTPS entrypoint and is scoped to port 443 only; the application tier behind it accepts traffic solely from this security group, at platform-infra/terraform/main.tf:95-101.

decoys.looks_like: Wildcard IAM action grant
decoys.ruled_out_by: The s3:* verb set is confined to one bucket by the resource list at platform-infra/terraform/iam.tf:27-30 and further restricted to a single gateway endpoint by the aws:SourceVpce condition at platform-infra/terraform/iam.tf:32-36.

decoys.looks_like: Database password checked into version control
decoys.ruled_out_by: The variable declares no default and is marked sensitive at platform-infra/terraform/variables.tf:42, so no value is stored here; it is supplied at run time from secrets at platform-infra/.github/workflows/deploy.yml:48.

decoys.looks_like: Downloading and running a remote binary in CI
decoys.ruled_out_by: The archive is verified against a pinned digest before it is unpacked, at platform-infra/.github/workflows/ci.yml:21 and :24, and the job holds only contents: read (platform-infra/.github/workflows/ci.yml:8-9).

decoys.looks_like: Server-side request forgery from a model-chosen URL
decoys.ruled_out_by: deskagent/agent/tools.py:39 requires https and line 41 requires the parsed hostname to be a member of the ALLOWED_HOSTS frozenset declared at deskagent/agent/tools.py:21-27, which is an exact-match set of three internal documentation hosts.

decoys.looks_like: Deserialization of attacker-controlled session data
decoys.ruled_out_by: The call is json.loads, not pickle, and the filename cannot be steered: _path rejects anything that is not a canonical uuid4 against SESSION_ID_RE at deskagent/agent/memory.py:39 (pattern at deskagent/agent/memory.py:21).

decoys.looks_like: Jailbreak instructions embedded in the assistant's prompt
decoys.ruled_out_by: The constant is an inert list of (attack, expected refusal) pairs; build_system_prompt at deskagent/agent/prompts.py:53-57 assembles the prompt from SYSTEM_PROMPT and CITATION_HINT only, and REFUSAL_EXAMPLES is referenced nowhere else in the tree.
